articles.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi US Senate seat, AP projects
articles.summary:
Democrat Scott Colom has won Mississippi's US Senate race, defeating Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith, according to projections by the Associated Press and other outlets on Wednesday US time. The result came after more than a week of counting in a race that had been too close to call since the 3 November election.

AP figures reported by WDAM put Colom on 49.2 per cent of the vote. Hyde-Smith has held the seat since 2018. Her response to the projection was not included in the AP report carried by WDAM.
keyFacts: Colom is a district attorney from Columbus, Mississippi
The race stayed too close to call for more than a week after polling day
The winner serves a six-year term

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to large prisoner swap; no breakthrough on ending the war
articles.summary:
Two days of US-mediated talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi ended on Wednesday with agreement on a large exchange of prisoners of war. Russia's chief negotiator, Vladimir Medinsky, said both sides had agreed to the swap. Ukraine's delegation was led by Rustem Umerov.

No ceasefire was agreed. US envoy Jared Kushner said territorial issues would be the hardest to settle but that progress was made on a post-war security framework. He said he and Steve Witkoff would travel to Moscow to brief Vladimir Putin and then meet Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin.
keyFacts: Final prisoner numbers had not been set when the talks ended
Russian state agency TASS said the exchange should happen within two to three weeks
It was the first meeting between the two delegations in about nine months

articles.title: US inflation comes in higher than forecast, raising odds of a Fed rate rise
articles.summary:
US consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which exclude food and energy, rose 0.3% against a forecast of 0.2%. The bureau could not publish annual figures because it collected no data in October 2025, during the government shutdown.

Fed Governor Christopher Waller said before the release that a half-point rate rise should be considered in December if core inflation came in around 0.3%. US shares and Treasuries fell after the data, and the ASX was expected to open lower.
keyFacts: Headline CPI +0.4% for the month; core +0.3%
September's headline rise was 0.6%
Markets raised the odds of a December rate hike

articles.title: NAB to repay $169m to 66,000 underpaid workers under Fair Work undertaking
articles.summary:
National Australia Bank has signed an enforceable undertaking with the Fair Work Ombudsman over underpayments affecting 65,999 current and former staff between 2012 and 2026, the regulator announced on Thursday. NAB will pay $127 million in wages, $34 million in interest and $8 million in superannuation.

The bank will also make a $2 million contrition payment to the Commonwealth, which the regulator described as the largest under such an undertaking. NAB self-reported the problems in late 2019. Fair Work Ombudsman Anna Booth criticised the bank's failure to build compliant payroll systems. The undertaking requires an independent payroll audit and reporting to the board.
keyFacts: Individual amounts range from under $5 to more than $87,000
NAB says it has already paid at least $155 million
No court penalty applies under an enforceable undertaking

articles.title: New home loans fall 15 per cent in September quarter, largest drop on record
articles.summary:
The number of new home loans in Australia fell 15.0 per cent to 111,878 in the September quarter, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Wednesday. The value of new loans fell 15.5 per cent to $81.2 billion, the largest quarterly fall since the series began in 2002.

New investor loans fell 30.6 per cent in number and 32.3 per cent in value, both record falls. ABS head of finance statistics Mish Tan said investor activity reflected more than borrowing costs, including possible tax changes and expectations of lower house prices. Workplace Relations Minister Amanda Rishworth told the ABC the data showed investors moving to new homes.
keyFacts: Owner-occupier loans fell 5.3 per cent
First home buyer loans fell 8.6 per cent
It was the third straight quarterly fall in investor loans

articles.title: Qantas to cut 850 corporate jobs in outsourcing deal with Accenture
articles.summary:
Qantas told staff on Tuesday it will cut 850 positions after signing an outsourcing deal with consultancy Accenture. The first phase covers finance, procurement, human resources and marketing, with the Sydney headquarters most affected. AAP reports most of Accenture's work for Qantas will be done in India, with some roles staying in Australia.

Chief executive Vanessa Hudson linked the move to modernising technology and the impact of AI. The Australian Services Union criticised the cuts as sending skills offshore. Transport Minister Catherine King called the decision extremely disappointing.
keyFacts: 850 positions; some reports put the total near 1,000
Qantas reported a $1.3 billion net profit for 2025/26 in August
Qantas says it will consult affected staff and redeploy where possible

articles.title: US House shelves Hegseth impeachment; Jordan to lead Republicans in new Congress
articles.summary:
The US House voted 211–204 to refer Republican Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to the Judiciary Committee, which effectively ends it for now. The articles accuse Hegseth of conducting hostilities against Iran without congressional authorisation. Massie was the only Republican to vote against the referral. Eleven Democrats and seven Republicans did not vote.

Separately, House Republicans elected Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise, 106–73 according to CBS News sources, to lead them when they become the minority in January.
keyFacts: Vote was on a motion to refer, not on impeachment itself
11 Democrats were absent; the margin was 7
Senate Republicans re-elected John Thune as leader

articles.title: ASIC sues Commonwealth Bank, alleging $8.5m in undisclosed business fees
articles.summary:
The Australian Securities and Investments Commission has started civil penalty proceedings against Commonwealth Bank over fees on its CommBiz business banking platform, according to ABC News and AAP. ASIC alleges about 42,000 business customers were overcharged about $8.5 million for direct debits and credits between November 2020 and May 2025.

ASIC alleges the platform's terms misled customers about fees from its 2006 launch, and that complaints began in 2015. Commissioner Alan Kirkland said the regulator alleges the bank broke a basic promise. CBA stopped the fees in 2025 and has paid $26.4 million in remediation to about 93,000 customers. CBA had not commented when the reports were published.
keyFacts: The claims are allegations and have not been tested in court
No case management hearing had been listed
ASIC says a 2016 internal audit flagged the issue

articles.title: Spain holds first general strike since 2012 over housing; unions claim four million joined
articles.summary:
Spain's two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, held a 24-hour general strike on Wednesday over housing costs and wages, the first general strike in the country since 2012. The unions said four million workers took part, according to Reuters reporting carried by ABC News. That figure has not been independently confirmed.

Police reported 40 arrests across 476 incidents by midday. Unions said they would file a criminal complaint over what they called a disproportionate police response. Employer group CEOE said the strike was counterproductive. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez faces a general election on 29 November.
keyFacts: Spain's central bank estimates a housing shortfall of about 750,000 homes
A BBVA Research economist estimated a 0.1–0.2 per cent hit to annual GDP
Basque broadcaster EITB reported 32 arrests in the early hours

articles.title: US charges three men over alleged Iran-backed plots in Europe and the US
articles.summary:
Federal prosecutors in New York unsealed an indictment charging three men over what they describe as a campaign of nearly 20 attacks targeting Jewish communities in Europe and the US, plus a plot against RAF Fairford, a British base used by US forces. Prosecutors allege the men acted for Iran's Revolutionary Guard and the Iraqi militia Kata'ib Hezbollah. Only one of the three, Mohammad Baqer al-Saadi, is in custody.

Iran has denied involvement in the Fairford incident. Separately, UK police arrested a US Army soldier on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence.
keyFacts: Three men charged; only al-Saadi is in custody
Al-Saadi pleaded not guilty in June to earlier charges
The UK soldier arrest is a separate case

articles.title: Israel's new parliament sworn in with no bloc holding a majority
articles.summary:
Israel's 26th Knesset was sworn in on Tuesday. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposing bloc holds the 61 seats needed to govern. President Isaac Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the first mandate to form a government on 8 November, giving him 28 days.

Netanyahu called on opposition parties to join a unity government under his leadership. Eisenkot's bloc sought a vote to replace Speaker Amir Ohana of Likud at the opening session. Ohana said such a vote required 61 signatures.
keyFacts: Likud is the largest party with 27 seats
Eisenkot has 28 days to form a coalition
ABC reported heckling during Netanyahu's speech

articles.title: Israeli strikes kill at least 10 in Gaza over two days, health officials say
articles.summary:
Israeli forces killed at least seven Palestinians in Gaza on Tuesday, including a father and his 13-year-old son, local health officials told Reuters. Medics said the two were killed when an airstrike hit the roof of a displacement shelter in Gaza City's Zeitoun neighbourhood. On Wednesday, strikes killed three more people, including two brothers at a tent for displaced people.

The Israeli military said it struck militants in the areas, without giving details. Gaza's Health Ministry says more than 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire began in October 2025.
keyFacts: At least 7 killed Tuesday and 3 Wednesday, per local health officials
The Israeli military says it targeted militants
The ceasefire took effect in October 2025

articles.title: Senior US soldier arrested in England on suspicion of aiding Russian intelligence
articles.summary:
A 41-year-old US Army soldier was arrested near Gloucester, England, on Tuesday on suspicion of offences under the UK's National Security Act, London's Metropolitan Police said. Counter-terrorism officers worked with the FBI and the US military, and searches were carried out at two addresses in Gloucestershire.

The man has not been named or charged. Brigadier General Sean Stinchon of US Army Counterintelligence Command described him as a senior soldier. FBI Director Kash Patel called it an important arrest. Police said the case is Russia-related and not linked to earlier Iran-related incidents at RAF Fairford.
keyFacts: The suspect is held in custody in London
The offences relate to two sections of the National Security Act 2023
Police called it a significant investigation

articles.title: Global fossil CO2 emissions projected to fall 0.4 per cent in 2026
articles.summary:
Carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are projected to fall 0.4 per cent in 2026 to 38.2 billion tonnes, according to the annual Global Carbon Budget released on Tuesday. The researchers said a projected 1.9 per cent fall in oil use was likely a short-term response to the energy shock from the Iran conflict.

Including land-use change, total emissions are projected to rise from 42.8 to 43.3 billion tonnes. Lead author Pierre Friedlingstein of the University of Exeter told AAP the fall was partly temporary. The report projects declines in China, the US and the EU, and a rise in India.
keyFacts: Projected changes: China −0.9%, US −1.3%, EU −1.5%, India +4.4%
The figures are projections, not final data
Australia's fossil emissions fell 1.2 per cent in 2025, the report found

articles.title: COP31: rooftop solar declaration unveiled; Australia was first to sign
articles.summary:
The Global Solar Council unveiled a Global Rooftop Solar Declaration at the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Turkey. Signatory governments commit to helping double the number of homes with rooftop solar, from about 150 million to 300 million, by 2030. The declaration is voluntary and non-binding.

Australia became the first country to endorse it in October, when Energy Minister Chris Bowen, who is COP31's president of negotiations, signed at a Pacific pre-COP meeting in Fiji. ABC reports negotiators are split over a separate electrification target.
keyFacts: COP31 runs 9–20 November in Antalya
Target: 300 million solar homes by 2030
More than a third of Australian homes have rooftop solar

articles.title: Albanese meets Erdoğan and Norway's Støre at COP31 leaders' summit
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has held talks with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Finnish President Alexander Stubb at the COP31 climate summit in Antalya, Türkiye, ABC News reported. Government readouts said the talks covered clean energy, AI, the Middle East and Ukraine.

At the leaders' summit, Albanese called for action to protect Pacific nations. UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for no new fossil fuel infrastructure. Critics accused Australia of continuing to expand coal and gas. Australia is leading the negotiations at COP31 under an arrangement with host Türkiye.
keyFacts: The Erdoğan meeting covered COP31 leadership and defence
The Støre meeting covered online and AI safety
Australia was the first to sign COP31's rooftop solar declaration

articles.title: Anthropic opens IPO share offer to Australian retail investors
articles.summary:
AI company Anthropic has lodged a prospectus with the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, opening part of its initial public offering to Australian retail investors, AAP and Bloomberg reported. The global offer is for 825 million shares at US$70 to US$78 each, with a Nasdaq listing planned for 20 November.

The Australian offer opened on Wednesday and closes on 17 November, with CommSec as lead broker. At the midpoint price the raise would be about US$84.6 billion, according to AAP's calculation. The prospectus reports a net loss of US$23.3 billion for the September quarter and says the investment carries a high degree of risk.
keyFacts: Final pricing is due on 19 November
Anthropic reported almost US$17 billion in September-quarter revenue
Eight Australian brokers are taking part

articles.title: Nvidia board investigates reports CEO was target of foreign intelligence effort
articles.summary:
Nvidia's board said on 8 November it was opening an independent investigation into reports that chief executive Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. A committee of independent directors with outside counsel will run it. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

The New York Times reported in October that US officials concluded Megaspeed executive Alice Huang was passing information to Beijing. China denies this. Jensen Huang told staff he had been unfaithful to his wife. Nvidia shares fell more than 4% on Monday.
keyFacts: Investigation is internal; no charges reported
Huang remains CEO and says he will cooperate
Shares closed at US$178.67 on 9 November

articles.title: House Republicans' Epstein report says federal government failed survivors
articles.summary:
Republicans on the US House Oversight Committee released a report on Tuesday concluding their 15-month investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. It found the federal government mishandled criminal investigations into Epstein over decades and failed survivors. It drew on 19 witness interviews and depositions and on documents subpoenaed from the Justice Department, Epstein's estate and two banks.

The report said the facts uncovered do not suggest President Trump was implicated in Epstein's crimes. It accused committee Democrats of trying to implicate him. It identified two former federal prosecutors whose role in the original case raised concerns, according to Fox News.
keyFacts: Report runs to about 136 pages
Released by the Republican majority under chair James Comer
Next steps are left to the Justice Department

articles.title: Hundreds of Italian schools evacuated after emailed bomb threats
articles.summary:
At least 300 schools in Italy were evacuated on Wednesday after emailed bomb warnings, Reuters reported in a story carried by ABC News. Schools in Scotland, Northern Ireland and Ireland received similar emails, which authorities classed as hoaxes and which did not disrupt classes.

Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto said the threats were intended to spread fear. No group has been confirmed as responsible. Russia denied involvement, and Iran called accusations against it baseless. The emails follow similar waves of hoax threats sent to schools in Europe in October and early November.
keyFacts: No explosives were reported found
Italian postal police have investigated earlier emails
France separately summoned Iran's ambassador over an alleged cyberattack

articles.title: RBA economist says AI investment is adding to demand before productivity gains show
articles.summary:
Reserve Bank chief economist Sarah Hunter said on Monday that AI is already reshaping the Australian economy through business investment and demand. AAP reports there is so far limited evidence that AI is lifting productivity. RBA staff estimate data centre investment has grown roughly tenfold in three years and project a further $115 billion by the end of 2028.

RBA research found households' exposure to AI-related shares, mostly through super, rose from about 2% of financial wealth in 2022 to 5.3% in June 2026. Staff estimate a 30% fall in those shares would cut household wealth by 1.6%.
keyFacts: Speech delivered 9 November in Sydney
AI-related memory chip prices rose more than 200% in a year, per RBA research
The $115 billion projection depends on power, water and construction capacity

articles.title: Victorian Liberals withdraw Williamstown candidate over comments on Indigenous people
articles.summary:
The Victorian Liberal Party has withdrawn its endorsement of Paul Lindemann, its candidate for the seat of Williamstown, over comments he made about Indigenous Australians, ABC News reported on Thursday. The party said it had not previously been aware of the comments.

Liberal leader Jess Wilson told ABC News Breakfast the comments were deeply offensive and that the party's vetting process had not detected them. The ABC said it had tried to contact Lindemann. Campaigning resumed on Thursday after a pause for Remembrance Day, ahead of the state election on 28 November.
keyFacts: Williamstown is in Melbourne's west
Wilson said she was disappointed by the vetting failure
Lindemann's response had not been reported

articles.title: Developer pauses 1,200MW AI data centre plan in Adelaide Hills
articles.summary:
Quantum DC has paused its proposal for a 1,200-megawatt AI data centre at Tungkillo in South Australia's Adelaide Hills, ABC News reported on Thursday. The company said it would not seek development approval this year but has not ruled out proceeding later.

Chief executive Alby Tomassi said in a statement the company had misread the strength of local feeling. More than 350 people contacted the company and residents submitted 432 questions. Planned community sessions have been cancelled, and the company said an independent expert panel would review its specialist studies.
keyFacts: Two earlier consultation sessions were postponed
The proposal included an energy hub
A community meeting was earlier cancelled over a bomb threat, Data Center Dynamics reported

articles.title: Report finds alcohol-related hepatitis rose in Victoria and remains elevated
articles.summary:
Hospital admissions for alcohol-associated hepatitis in Victoria rose sharply during the COVID-19 pandemic and remain elevated, according to a Burnet Institute report commissioned by the Foundation for Alcohol Research and Education (FARE), ABC News reported.

Lead author Professor Jessica Howell said about 40 per cent of admissions between 2017 and 2024 were people under 45. About 13 per cent of patients were admitted to intensive care, and the mortality rate was about 4 per cent. Women made up about one in three cases. The study was retrospective and drew on two Victorian patient databases.
keyFacts: FARE is an alcohol-harm advocacy group
The study covered 2017 to 2024
An independent hepatologist commented on the findings to the ABC

articles.title: Nvidia board meets on Jensen Huang's future after reports it may remove him
articles.summary:
Nvidia's board met on Wednesday, US time, to consider chief executive Jensen Huang's future, Reuters reported, citing a source. The Wall Street Journal first reported the board was preparing to remove him, and CBS News said two sources gave the same account. Nvidia had not commented, and no decision had been announced by Thursday evening Sydney time.

This is new since the board opened its investigation on 8 November. The New York Times has since reported, citing five people, that Huang had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia vice-president. That followed earlier reports about his ties to Alice Huang, whom US officials suspect of working for Beijing. China denies this. Shares fell about 8 per cent after hours.
keyFacts: Nvidia has not confirmed the reports that the board plans to remove him
Shares fell about 8% in after-hours trade on Wednesday
A House committee chair said he may subpoena Huang

articles.title: Russia and Ukraine trade strikes on capitals as US envoys arrive in Moscow
articles.summary:
Russia and Ukraine attacked each other's capitals early on Thursday, a day after US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi ended, Reuters reported. A Reuters witness heard explosions in Kyiv. Russia's defence ministry said it hit military and energy sites and a munitions store in Kyiv. Moscow's mayor said five drones heading for the city were shot down.

US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff landed in Moscow for a meeting with Vladimir Putin and were greeted by Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev. They then plan to fly to Ireland to meet Volodymyr Zelensky. US mediators say the two sides still disagree on major issues, including territory.
keyFacts: Kyiv Independent reported explosions in Kyiv at about 1am local time
Officials in Rivne region reported damage to energy infrastructure
Kushner said European partners must take part in the talks

articles.title: Israeli strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital kills six, health ministry says
articles.summary:
An Israeli airstrike hit Nasser Hospital in Khan Younis, southern Gaza, early on Thursday, killing six people and wounding at least 12, according to Gaza's Health Ministry. The ministry said the strike hit the surgery department and that a doctor was among those killed. An AP journalist at the scene said parts of the second floor were destroyed.

The Israeli military said it targeted a senior Hamas militant and others, without giving evidence. Israel accuses Hamas of using hospitals as cover, which Hamas denies. Nasser is one of the few hospitals still working in Gaza.
keyFacts: Casualty figures come from Gaza's Health Ministry
The Israeli military said the target was a senior Hamas figure
The strike follows two days of deadly strikes reported earlier this week

articles.title: Iran says it hit navigation systems on Omani island; tanker reported on fire in Hormuz
articles.summary:
Three sources told Reuters that Iran attacked shipping navigation systems on Oman's Didamar island in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media said the Revolutionary Guards destroyed what it called enemy navigation systems there. Reuters could not confirm whether anything was destroyed, and shipping sources said the effect on commercial traffic was likely to be limited.

Separately, Iran's army said on Wednesday an oil tanker hit a mine and caught fire after entering a restricted area. The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency said it had a report of an incident involving a tanker, with damage and crew condition unknown. US Central Command and Oman did not comment.
keyFacts: It is unclear whether the two tanker reports refer to the same ship
Iran has restricted Hormuz traffic since the war began in late February
The US says mines in the area have been cleared

articles.title: Queensland CFMEU inquiry calls for building code; Miles apologises for Labor policy
articles.summary:
The commission of inquiry into the Queensland CFMEU released an interim report early, citing an urgent need for change, the ABC reported. Commissioner Stuart Wood KC recommended a new construction industry code and a dedicated regulator, with exclusion from government-funded work as the main penalty. He found Labor's Best Practice Industry Conditions policy raised costs by at least 20 per cent on three major projects.

On Thursday, Opposition Leader Steven Miles apologised for the 2018 policy, saying it was misused and he would not bring it back. Deputy Premier Jarrod Bleijie said the apology did not go far enough. He said the government was considering the report and had already committed to a code.
keyFacts: The cost finding covers Cross River Rail, Centenary Bridge and Gold Coast Light Rail
The final report is now due in December 2027
The Crisafulli government suspended the policy in 2024

articles.title: Victorian pre-election budget update forecasts wider deficit and slower growth
articles.summary:
Victoria's Department of Treasury and Finance released its pre-election budget update on Thursday, ahead of the 28 November state election, AAP reported. It forecasts the cash deficit widening by $3 billion over four years compared with the May budget, and net debt reaching $196.2 billion by mid-2030.

The update forecasts economic growth slowing to 1 per cent this financial year, down from 1.5 per cent in May, and unemployment rising to 5.25 per cent. It cites higher interest rates, persistent inflation and federal migration cuts. Premier Ben Carroll said he would cut spending, while Opposition Leader Jess Wilson has set a goal of a cash surplus by 2032.
keyFacts: Operating surplus forecast at $700 million for 2026-27, down $400 million
Prepared by the public service under caretaker rules
Victorians vote on 28 November

articles.title: David Jones to close 19 of its 38 stores under receivers' plan
articles.summary:
Receivers for David Jones announced on Wednesday plans to close 19 of the department store chain's 38 stores, the ABC reported. Chief executive Erica Berchtold told suppliers in an email that the store network was no longer the right shape for the business. She said the stores were expected to trade through the Christmas period, with final trading days later in the year.

David Jones went into voluntary administration last week, with McGrath Nicol appointed administrator. Employment Minister Amanda Rishworth urged the company to redeploy affected staff. The number of jobs affected has not been announced.
keyFacts: The store network covers Australia and New Zealand
FTI Consulting is receiver for lender Hilco
Exact closing dates have not been set

articles.title: Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 11,000 cases, government data show
articles.summary:
Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of Congo have passed 11,000, according to government health data reported by Reuters and AP. The figures show 11,042 infections and 5,387 deaths since the outbreak was declared in mid-May. It is caused by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there is no approved vaccine or treatment.

The outbreak has spread to eight of Congo's 26 provinces, with Ituri and North Kivu the main hotspots, and cases have been reported in Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria. Reuters said delayed detection, conflict and strained health services have helped it spread. Only the 2014-16 West African outbreak has been larger.
keyFacts: Deaths are close to half of recorded infections
The outbreak was declared in mid-May 2026
AP reported attacks on health workers and facilities

articles.title: ANZ chief tells parliament inquiry global markets are in a 'dangerous situation'
articles.summary:
ANZ chief executive Nuno Matos told a parliamentary inquiry in Canberra on Thursday that record share prices combined with high interest rates were a dangerous mix for the world, the ABC reported. He linked strong competition for capital to spending on AI and data centres, government spending and persistent inflation.

Matos said he expected the Australian economy to slow noticeably but not go into recession. He said a sudden halt in AI spending would cause major global problems, but he did not expect one. He also called for rules on AI, citing fraud risks. The other major bank chiefs are due to appear before the committee.
keyFacts: The inquiry is chaired by Labor MP Ed Husic
Matos reported a $7.59 billion cash profit for ANZ
NAB and CBA chiefs are due to appear on Friday

articles.title: Australia expected to run out of Q fever vaccine this week
articles.summary:
Australia is expected to run out of Q-VAX, its only Q fever vaccine, this week, ABC Rural reported. Supplier CSL Seqirus said it expects a short, temporary stock-out until the end of the year. It said the next two batches have been sped up and are expected in late December.

The company blamed raw material supply problems and equipment faults on its filling lines, which meant three or four batches could not be released. Each batch takes about nine months to make. Farmers told the ABC they had been unable to vaccinate staff for months. The Health Department said CSL Seqirus manages supply under a 10-year, $1 billion arrangement.
keyFacts: 991 Q fever cases were recorded last year, a record
Q fever spreads from livestock to people
Supply is expected to improve early next year

articles.title: Yemen fighting intensifies as Saudi Arabia and Houthis trade missile and drone claims
articles.summary:
The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted three cruise missiles aimed at Riyadh and drones aimed at Mecca and southern Saudi Arabia, Al Jazeera reported. Saudi civil defence said debris from intercepted missiles fell in a village in Mecca province. A Houthi spokesperson denied targeting Mecca and said the group struck a pumping station in Yanbu and targeted Riyadh's airport.

The WHO said that as of 8 November the fighting had caused 11,755 casualties, including 2,098 deaths. It said more than 320,000 people had been displaced since 1 August. Yemen's government-aligned army said at least 138 Houthi fighters were killed or wounded; this has not been independently verified.
keyFacts: Casualty and displacement figures are from the WHO
Each side's claims about the strikes have not been independently confirmed
More than 2,000 casualties were recorded in nine days

articles.title: Taiwan says it is attending China-hosted APEC summit on an 'equal basis'
articles.summary:
Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te said on Thursday that Taiwan is taking part in next week's APEC leaders' summit in Shenzhen, China, on an equal basis with other members, Reuters reported. His government had earlier asked Beijing for a written guarantee. Lai named Acer founder Stan Shih as Taiwan's envoy.

China's foreign ministry said it handles the participation of what it calls the Taiwan region under the one-China principle and APEC's agreed rules. It said Taiwan's representatives can attend as normal if those practices are followed. US President Donald Trump is expected to meet Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.
keyFacts: Shih was also Taiwan's envoy at the 2007 APEC summit in Sydney
Taiwan usually sends business leaders or former officials to APEC
Beijing refuses to talk to Lai and claims Taiwan as its territory

articles.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia chief executive; CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO
articles.summary:
Nvidia's board said on Thursday US time that co-founder Jensen Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and director, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while the board searches for a permanent replacement, and former Synopsys chief Harvey Jones becomes the company's first board chair. The company's statement gave no reason.

The move follows a board investigation into reports, first published by The New York Times, about Huang's personal relationships and possible foreign intelligence interest, according to AP and ABC News. China denies the spying claims. AP reported President Trump suggested former Apple CEO Tim Cook as a successor. Nvidia shares fell about 5 per cent by midday.
keyFacts: Huang led Nvidia for 33 years
Nvidia reports quarterly results on 17 November
A proposed class action alleges shareholders were misled; the claim is untested

articles.title: Kremlin says Putin's talks with US envoys were constructive; trilateral talks to continue
articles.summary:
Russian President Vladimir Putin met US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Moscow on Thursday to discuss ending the war in Ukraine, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said, according to Reuters and Ukrainian agency UNN. Ushakov described the talks as substantive and useful and said the sides agreed to continue three-way negotiations with Ukraine.

Ushakov said the envoys supported a humanitarian mission in Kostiantynivka. The US side had not released its own account in the reports reviewed. The envoys were next due to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Dublin. Russian Deputy Foreign Minister Sergei Ryabkov said it was too soon to say trust had been restored after this week's Abu Dhabi talks.
keyFacts: The Moscow meeting followed two days of talks in Abu Dhabi
The Kremlin's description has not been independently confirmed
No date has been announced for the Dublin meeting

articles.title: Iran says four tankers hit by explosions in Strait of Hormuz after ignoring warnings
articles.summary:
Iran's military said on Thursday that four oil tankers had been struck by explosions in the Strait of Hormuz after entering restricted areas, Reuters reported. The Revolutionary Guards navy said two supertankers were disabled on Wednesday, and Iran's army later said two more hit mines in the eastern part of the strait on Thursday afternoon.

Reuters said it could not immediately verify Iran's account. Separately, the UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said a vessel was hit by an unidentified projectile about 14 nautical miles north-west of Ras Al-Khaimah on Wednesday, causing an engine-room fire; the crew were evacuated. Iranian state media said vessels had struck naval mines.
keyFacts: Iran says the ships used an unauthorised route
At least 10 ships were hit in the first 10 days of November, per the Washington Institute
October had 37 recorded attacks, the most of any month in the conflict

articles.title: Israeli cabinet reportedly orders military to prepare for possible Iran strike
articles.summary:
Israel's security cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, ordered the military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli broadcaster KAN reported on Wednesday evening, according to Al Jazeera. The Israeli government had not confirmed the report.

Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said any base used in a new US war would be a legitimate target. President Trump has said he is prepared to resume the war if a Qatar-backed diplomatic track fails. Israeli opposition figure Gadi Eisenkot urged against action without a direct and immediate threat. Al Jazeera said Tehran had rejected a US proposal to move its highly enriched uranium to a third country.
keyFacts: The report came from Israeli public broadcaster KAN
Brent crude settled at US$92.76 a barrel on Wednesday
Iran rejects sending enriched uranium abroad

articles.title: ASIO and AFP open $76m online counter-terrorism centre in Sydney
articles.summary:
A new Counter Terrorism Online Centre combining ASIO and the Australian Federal Police opens in Sydney on Friday, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said, according to ABC News and AAP. The centre, funded in the May federal budget, will monitor online radicalisation and act as a single contact point for overseas agencies.

Burke said ASIO had found an Australian Discord server with more than 1,000 members spreading extremist ideology. AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett described the centre as an early-warning system. ASIO director-general Mike Burgess said his agency and partners needed to be online too. ABC reported children make up 40 per cent of this year's counter-terrorism caseload.
keyFacts: ABC put the cost at $76 million; AAP reported $74 million
It builds on existing cybercrime and child exploitation hubs
A 17-year-old NSW boy was charged with a terrorism offence the day before

articles.title: Microsoft Outlook, Teams and 365 hit by global outage
articles.summary:
Microsoft confirmed an outage on Thursday US time that left many users unable to reach their Outlook inboxes, TechCrunch reported. The problem was first reported in the Americas and Microsoft later said it could affect any region. Users also reported problems with Teams, Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services, according to Euronews and ABC News.

Microsoft said part of its infrastructure was under higher than normal load and that it was redistributing traffic. It did not give a cause. Downdetector recorded more than 130,000 Outlook reports at the peak, Euronews said, though such counts may not match the number of people affected. Microsoft said Teams had been restored in North America.
keyFacts: Exchange Online mailboxes could not be reached
Microsoft had a days-long 365 outage in September
No cause has been given

articles.title: Pacific leaders press for climate finance as Albanese meets them at COP31
articles.summary:
Prime Minister Anthony Albanese met Pacific leaders at the COP31 climate summit in Turkey on Thursday, as the Pacific Resilience Facility reached US$200 million towards a US$500 million target, AAP reported. Businessman Andrew Forrest announced a US$5 million contribution.

Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr called for funding rather than promises. Climate Minister Chris Bowen said only 0.2 per cent of global climate finance reaches small island states. Greenpeace Australia Pacific called on Australia to commit to ending new fossil fuel projects. Asked about criticism from activist Greta Thunberg, Albanese said she was entitled to her views. Australia is co-hosting the summit with Turkey.
keyFacts: The facility is a Pacific-run fund for climate resilience
It has raised US$200 million of a US$500 million goal
Australia leads COP31 negotiations while Turkey hosts

articles.title: ABC analysis finds 40 medicines in critical shortage, 13 of them repeatedly
articles.summary:
An ABC News analysis of Therapeutic Goods Administration data going back to 2015 found 40 medicines are currently in critical shortage in Australia, and 13 of those have been critically short more than once. The penicillin injection Bicillin L-A has been in critical shortage since April 2025, which its supplier attributes to manufacturing problems.

The pancreatic enzyme treatment Creon has been short for more than a year amid higher demand, the ABC reported. Professor John Saunders of the Royal Australasian College of Physicians said doctors were frustrated. The TGA said it cannot force companies to supply medicines. Australia is also expected to run out of Q fever vaccine this week.
keyFacts: Analysis covers TGA shortage records since 2015
40 medicines are in critical shortage
The TGA says it has no power to compel supply

articles.title: Released EPA data show 1,907 tonnes of farmed salmon died in Macquarie Harbour
articles.summary:
Tasmanian Environment Protection Authority data released under right-to-information laws show 1,907 tonnes of farmed salmon died in Macquarie Harbour between October 2024 and December 2025, ABC News reported. The data were obtained by Environment Tasmania and released after salmon companies sought reviews of the decision.

Environment Tasmania's Jess Coughlan described the death rates as very high. Salmon Tasmania chief John Whittington said fewer than 8 per cent of fish held had died and that tonnage could not be used as a mortality rate. The harbour farms' environmental licences expired almost a year ago; the companies have applied for renewal and can keep operating while applications are assessed.
keyFacts: Covers October 2024 to December 2025
Industry says under 8 per cent of fish died
Licence renewals are still being assessed

articles.title: NSW Premier and ministers subpoenaed in Herzog protest policing case
articles.summary:
Lawyers for protesters charged after clashes with police at a February rally in Sydney against Israeli President Isaac Herzog's visit have subpoenaed NSW Premier Chris Minns, Police Minister Yasmin Catley, Tourism Minister Steve Kamper and Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon, AAP reported on Thursday.

Solicitor Nick Hanna, who represents 16 people, said he would argue the policing was unlawful. Spokespeople declined to comment because the matter is before the courts. The Law Enforcement Conduct Commission is still investigating. AAP said the charges are under review after the Court of Appeal ruled protest restrictions in place at the time unconstitutional. The allegations against police have not been tested.
keyFacts: The rally was at Sydney Town Hall on 9 February
16 clients are represented by one lawyer
The LECC investigation is ongoing

articles.title: Australia signs agreement to join EU's Horizon Europe research program
articles.summary:
Industry and Science Minister Tim Ayres signed an agreement in Brussels with EU research commissioner Ekaterina Zaharieva for Australia to join Horizon Europe, the EU's main research funding program, AAP reported. Australian researchers will be able to take part from 1 January.

The government says the program is worth about $155 billion. The federal government contributed $20 million, matched by the Group of Eight universities, AAP said. Treaty negotiations were concluded earlier this year, according to Ayres' office. Canada, New Zealand and the UK are among more than 20 associated countries. Ayres said the deal links Australian researchers with leading international expertise.
keyFacts: Participation begins on 1 January 2027
Federal funding of $20m is matched by the Group of Eight
More than 20 countries are associated

articles.title: Victorian Labor to run open preference tickets in Prahran and Caulfield
articles.summary:
Victorian Labor will not recommend preferences after its own candidates in the seats of Prahran and Caulfield at the 28 November state election, AAP reported. Greens leader Ellen Sandell said the decision would help conservative candidates and called it unforgivable.

Prahran is held by Liberal MP Rachel Westaway, who won it from the Greens at a 2025 by-election that Labor did not contest. Opposition Leader Jess Wilson said the Liberals would put Labor, the Greens and the Victorian Socialists last, with decisions made seat by seat. A Resolve poll in The Age put the Coalition on 30 per cent of the primary vote, One Nation on 23, Labor on 22 and the Greens on 13.
keyFacts: The election is on 28 November
Open tickets give no preference recommendation
Liberals will set preferences seat by seat

articles.title: Iran says it struck US early-warning radar in Bahrain
articles.summary:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a US early-warning radar site in Bahrain, describing the strike as retaliation for an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Hormozgan province, Al Jazeera reported. Iranian state media said the port city of Sirik was hit on Thursday. The IRGC-affiliated Fars agency said the radar was destroyed.

The United States and Bahrain had not commented. Reuters said it was the first attack on US military assets in a Gulf country claimed by Iran since early September. US Central Command said its naval blockade of Iranian ports remained in force.
keyFacts: The IRGC called the strike a warning
Neither Washington nor Manama commented
The US blockade of Iranian ports continues

articles.title: Trump says US does not need Iran deal, tells Vance to focus on Democratic-run cities
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said the United States does not need a deal with Iran and directed Vice-President JD Vance to give his full attention to what Trump described as crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states, Reuters reported via the ABC. Trump wrote that the US held large sums of Iranian money and controlled the Strait of Hormuz.

The Wall Street Journal had reported that Vance was considering face-to-face talks with a senior Iranian security official; Reuters did not confirm this. Vance's office did not respond to requests for comment. Oil prices rose after the remarks, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Trump said a deal with Iran was not needed
Vance had been leading US contacts on Iran
Brent crude rose to about US$96 a barrel

articles.title: Microsoft services recovering; company says no sign outage was a cyber attack
articles.summary:
Microsoft said there was no indication that Friday's global outage of Outlook, Teams and other services was caused by a cyber attack, and reported a gradual recovery from about 10am AEDT, the ABC reported. Microsoft said a process that sets up secure connections on affected servers became overloaded and that it was reviewing recent configuration changes.

The AFP, ASIO, NSW Parliament, Service NSW and Queensland Health were among those affected, according to AAP. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said an agreement with Microsoft to prioritise Australian recovery had been activated. The ABC reported a senior Home Affairs official had warned in August about the impact of a Microsoft outage.
keyFacts: The outage began just after 3am AEDT
National Cyber Security Coordinator is examining it
Government agencies including AFP and ASIO were affected

articles.title: Finland detects strike on Russian warship in Gulf of Finland; Ukraine claims attack
articles.summary:
Finland's military said it detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and that Finland faced no immediate military threat, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters. Finland gave no details on the location or source. Finnish broadcaster Yle reported that Ukraine's Security Service said it carried out the attack.

Local media said the vessel was a small navy ship that returned to St Petersburg; casualties were unclear. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Ireland after talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow. Kushner said the US was working towards the war's largest prisoner exchange.
keyFacts: Finland said it faced no immediate threat
Ukraine's SBU claimed the attack, according to Yle
Russia said it intercepted 146 drones over Leningrad region

articles.title: Trump says he would consider military force against Cuba before leaving office
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump said in a radio interview with host Hugh Hewitt that he would consider using military force against Cuba and wanted to resolve the issue before his term ends in 2029, Al Jazeera reported. Politico reported it was the first time Trump had given a timeframe for a possible operation. Trump said Secretary of State Marco Rubio would support it.

A US oil blockade of Cuba has been in place since January. Cuban officials have called it collective punishment, and the island has faced nationwide blackouts and shortages. In March, the head of US Southern Command told senators US troops were not rehearsing an invasion.
keyFacts: Trump's term ends in January 2029
A US oil blockade has applied since January
The US has sanctioned President Díaz-Canel

articles.title: Government reconsidering planned backpacker visa changes, Burke indicates
articles.summary:
Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke indicated the government is reworking its planned changes to working holiday visas, the ABC reported. Burke said Australia still needed to reduce numbers and that the overall migration figure he announced could not change, but described the adjustments as tweaks and said a resolution was close.

Home Affairs data show British working holiday arrivals rose from 47,238 in 2023-24 to 79,412 in 2024-25, after a free trade deal removed specified work requirements for UK citizens. The ACCI said businesses needed certainty. Albanese raised the scheme with UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham at COP31, according to AAP.
keyFacts: Applications from 24 countries were paused in August
Labor targets net migration of 225,000 by 2028
UK citizens can stay up to three years

articles.title: UN Indigenous rights envoy says youth detention is creating a new Stolen Generation
articles.summary:
The UN Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples, Albert Barume, said at the end of his visit to Australia that the detention of Aboriginal children amounted to a new Stolen Generation, AAP reported. He said he was refused access to Darwin's Holtze and Queensland's Cleveland youth detention centres, and called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to show leadership.

A Senate report found that in the June 2025 quarter, 60 per cent of children in detention were Indigenous, compared with 6.6 per cent of the population. Barume is due to report to the UN Human Rights Council in September 2027.
keyFacts: Barume's visit ended on Friday
He said he was denied access to two centres
His report is due in September 2027

articles.title: APRA to run AI stress tests, says financial disruption is likely
articles.summary:
Australian Prudential Regulation Authority chair John Lonsdale said it was safe to assume artificial intelligence would cause interruptions and problems for banks, insurers and super funds, the ABC reported. APRA plans AI-focused stress tests of hypothetical severe scenarios from next year, and Lonsdale said major institutions were not yet adequately prepared.

APRA's System Risk Outlook, released on Thursday, placed AI at the centre of risks to the financial system, according to the ABC. In April, APRA wrote to industry leaders about cyber threats from frontier AI models, and in August APRA and ASIC jointly urged firms to move from awareness to action.
keyFacts: Stress tests are planned from next year
APRA's System Risk Outlook was released Thursday
ASIC and APRA issued a joint warning in August

articles.title: ASX falls nearly 1 per cent at midday; Australian dollar at lowest since January
articles.summary:
The S&P/ASX 200 was down 83.4 points, or 0.91 per cent, at 9,063.4 at midday on Friday, AAP reported, with financials down more than 1 per cent. A Capital.com analyst said Nvidia's leadership upheaval had slowed a recovery in technology shares.

Brent crude rose to about US$96 a barrel after President Trump's comments on Iran talks, while gold fell to a 13-month low near US$3,883 an ounce and copper reached its lowest level since July. The Australian dollar traded at 68.02 US cents, its lowest since January, according to AAP.
keyFacts: ASX 200 at midday: 9,063.4
Gold at a 13-month low
Australian dollar: 68.02 US cents

articles.title: Death toll from Brooklyn building collapse rises to at least eight
articles.summary:
At least eight people, including two children, died when a three-storey building collapsed into a neighbouring construction site in the Flatbush area of Brooklyn, New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani said, according to Al Jazeera. At least 18 people were taken to hospital, four in a critical condition, and about 250 firefighters attended.

The Fire Department said the cause was under investigation. City records cited in the report show a stop-work order was issued for the adjacent site in March, work resumed in violation in April, and it was allowed to continue in May. The architect, owner and contractor did not respond to AP.
keyFacts: The collapse happened on Wednesday afternoon local time
At least 18 people were hospitalised
A stop-work order was issued in March

articles.title: Spanish court suspends far-right group Núcleo Nacional in hate crime probe
articles.summary:
A judge in the northern Spanish city of Gijón suspended the activities of the far-right group Núcleo Nacional on Thursday, ordering its office closed and its social media and bank accounts blocked as part of an investigation into alleged hate crimes and illegal association, Al Jazeera reported, citing Reuters.

Fourteen members were arrested last week on suspicion of inciting hatred, and police said they seized more than 20 firearms from the group's Madrid headquarters. A representative of the group said in a video that it faced political persecution. Spain holds a general election on 29 November.
keyFacts: 14 members were arrested last week
Police seized more than 20 firearms
Spain votes on 29 November

articles.title: Bowen says coal and gas exports do not weaken Australia's role as COP31 negotiator
articles.summary:
Climate Change Minister Chris Bowen, who is presiding over COP31 negotiations in Türkiye, told the ABC that Australia's coal and gas exports had not undermined its standing as a negotiator and that countries needed a pragmatic energy transition. He said his role was to reach the most ambitious outcome that consensus would allow.

Bowen rejected criticism from activist Greta Thunberg and from Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, who has questioned the summit's costs. Australia is promoting a target to raise electricity's share of global energy use from about 23 per cent to 35 per cent by 2035; critics note it does not require renewables.
keyFacts: More than 190 countries are negotiating
The electrification target is 35 per cent by 2035
Negotiations intensify next week

articles.title: NSW inquiry hears from Bondi attack survivor and gun sellers on firearm law repeal bill
articles.summary:
Bondi terror attack survivor Leon Elski told a NSW parliamentary inquiry into a bill to repeal the state's new gun restrictions that he supported the reforms and stronger licence checks, AAP reported. He said the existing system had failed despite several layers of checks.

Gun retailers told the inquiry the changes, including a cap on firearms per person and a buyback, were damaging their businesses. The Shooters Union and the Australian Jewish Association backed repeal. Premier Chris Minns introduced the restrictions after the 14 December 2025 attack, in which 15 people were killed.
keyFacts: The inquiry is examining a repeal bill
Reforms include a per-person firearms cap
The Bondi attack killed 15 people

articles.title: SA energy minister supports gas helping power proposed AI data centres
articles.summary:
South Australian Energy Minister Tom Koutsantonis told the ABC he was comfortable with gas being used to firm power supply for proposed AI data centres when solar and wind output is low. The state's data centre strategy, released about five months ago, focused on renewable energy.

SA Greens leader Rob Simms called the position a reversal and proposed a moratorium, which a government spokesperson rejected. The Conservation Council called gas a step backwards, while Data Centres Australia defended its use. Developer Quantum DC paused its 1,200-megawatt Tungkillo proposal on 12 November.
keyFacts: Quantum DC estimated 20 per cent gas use
Iren has proposed an 800MW site at Bundey
The Greens want a data centre moratorium

articles.title: Senate inquiry told PM's honorary golf club membership was worth $1,100 a year
articles.summary:
Marrickville Golf Club president Andrew Tighe told a Senate inquiry on Thursday that Prime Minister Anthony Albanese had held an honorary membership since 2012, with privileges valued at $1,100 in 2026, AAP reported. Albanese has said it was worth about $5. MPs must declare gifts over $750, and the membership was not declared.

Club records show Albanese resigned the membership in September. The club received a $6 million grant from a $560 million invitation-only program. Opposition Leader Angus Taylor accused the Prime Minister of lying; the club's general manager described the valuation as an estimate.
keyFacts: The membership dated from 2012
The gift declaration threshold is $750
The club received a $6 million grant

articles.title: Big Build royal commission told state authority withheld Andrews-linked documents
articles.summary:
Counsel assisting Victoria's Big Build royal commission, Chris Young KC, said on Thursday that the Victorian Infrastructure Delivery Authority had produced documents late and incompletely, AAP reported. Text messages referring to former premier Daniel Andrews' office were provided only on Tuesday, and handwritten notes by a former Rail Projects Victoria chief were heavily redacted until repeated requests.

Young said state entities engaged only when compelled. The commission will seek evidence from two further witnesses. The hearings come ahead of the 28 November state election.
keyFacts: Texts were provided only on Tuesday
Notes were redacted until repeated requests
Two further witnesses will be sought

articles.title: NSW Supreme Court allows Rising Tide flotilla on Newcastle Harbour
articles.summary:
NSW Supreme Court Justice Edward Muston dismissed a police application to prohibit Rising Tide's anti-coal flotilla on Newcastle Harbour, finding the public interest in political expression outweighed the commissioner's safety concerns, the ABC reported. The protest is capped at 785 watercraft and will block the shipping channel for 30 to 40 minutes.

Police argued the risk of collision, capsize and drowning was serious. Rising Tide's barrister pointed to safety teams and mandatory life jackets, and an organiser said there would be no civil disobedience.
keyFacts: The ruling was made on Friday
Up to 785 watercraft may take part
The channel will be blocked for up to 40 minutes

articles.title: Storms with gusts up to 120km/h cut power to 25,500 homes south of Brisbane
articles.summary:
Thunderstorms with wind gusts of up to 120km/h struck south of Brisbane on Thursday, AAP reported. Energex said about 25,500 homes were without power by mid-afternoon, with hundreds of powerlines down, and 14 properties were left temporarily uninhabitable.

The SES received more than 300 calls for help, almost 240 of them in Logan, and more than 20 schools and several roads were closed. The Bureau of Meteorology said further thunderstorms and flash flooding were possible into the weekend.
keyFacts: Up to 100mm of rain fell in places
More than 300 calls were made to the SES
More storms are forecast into the weekend

articles.title: Tasmanian Premier apologises for effect of post about school Christmas events
articles.summary:
Tasmanian Premier Jeremy Rockliff apologised for the effect of an October Facebook post that said Christmas references were being removed from school celebrations, the ABC reported. The school concerned was identified online, called security over abuse, and its acting principal took leave.

The Australian Education Union had passed a no-confidence motion in Rockliff and barred politicians from school events until he apologised. The Education Department secretary had written to Rockliff on the day of the post saying Christmas remained important. Rockliff said he stood by his expectations and did not retract the claim.
keyFacts: The post was made on 14 October
The AEU passed a no-confidence motion
Rockliff did not withdraw the claim

articles.title: AAP FactCheck finds overseas-run pages invented Albanese–Allan feud
articles.summary:
AAP FactCheck found false a claim that former Victorian premier Jacinta Allan publicly called for Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to be removed. The posts came from a Facebook page that Meta's transparency data shows is run from Vietnam.

AAP said there was no record of such a statement. It also found no Hansard record of a claimed exchange between Bob Katter and Fatima Payman, and said a reported on-air clash between Albanese and Michael Rowland did not occur; Rowland left the ABC in February. Similar claims appeared on other pages ahead of the 28 November Victorian election.
keyFacts: The page is run from Vietnam, Meta data show
Allan lost the Labor leadership in July
Images showed signs of AI generation

leftOut.title: Iran repeats it will not send enriched uranium abroad; US keeps focus on sanctions
leftOut.summary:
Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, said again this week that none of Iran's enriched nuclear material will leave the country. He first made the statement publicly on 20 October during a visit by Pakistan's army chief, Asim Munir.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has said economic pressure, including a naval blockade, has reduced the need for major combat. Axios first reported in August that Rubio told allies the US was shifting from strikes to sanctions, without ruling out force if Iran attacks first.
keyFacts: Iran says its enriched material is for use only inside the country
US strategy: naval blockade plus Treasury sanctions
Both positions have been stated before

leftOut.title: Digital duty of care bill awaits Senate committee report due 20 November
leftOut.summary:
The Online Safety Amendment (Digital Duty of Care) Bill 2026 passed the House of Representatives on 28 October and is now before the Senate. It would place a legal duty on online services, including social media, search engines and generative AI services, to take reasonable steps to keep Australians safe, with extra protections for under-18s.

Companies that breach the duty could face penalties of up to about $109 million. The government has backed changes aimed at AI chatbots that simulate emotional intimacy with children. The Greens want stronger penalties.
keyFacts: Introduced by Communications Minister Anika Wells
Passed the House on 28 October
Senate committee report due 20 November

leftOut.title: Pope Leo draws an estimated 2.5 million to Buenos Aires Mass on first papal visit to Argentina since 1987
leftOut.summary:
Pope Leo XIV celebrated an open-air Mass in Buenos Aires on 9 November that officials estimated drew 2.5 million people, the largest gathering of his papacy. The same day he met victims of clergy abuse. He celebrated Mass in Córdoba on 10 November and visited Luján on 11 November.

It is the first papal visit to Argentina since 1987. The 12-day trip also covers Uruguay and Peru and ends on 17 November.
keyFacts: Argentina leg ran 8–11 November
The Pope met President Javier Milei during the visit
Next stop: Peru

leftOut.title: Khawaja memoir claims whole Australian team knew about 2018 ball-tampering plan
leftOut.summary:
Former Test opener Usman Khawaja claims in his memoir Sabr that the whole Australian team knew of the 2018 ball-tampering plan in Cape Town. He also says similar tactics were discussed during the previous Test in Port Elizabeth. That contradicts the Cricket Australia investigation, which found only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft knew.

Khawaja told captain Pat Cummins and Cricket Australia chief Todd Greenberg about the chapter before the team's South Africa tour. AAP reported he has since cut back some book-tour appearances.
keyFacts: Book published by Penguin Australia in November
The 2018 investigation named only three players
Other players' accounts differ from Khawaja's

leftOut.title: David Walliams faces further allegations; he denies wrongdoing
leftOut.summary:
Comedian and children's author David Walliams faced further allegations this week of inappropriate behaviour towards young women, in reporting by The Guardian and ITV. HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025 after an internal investigation, and in September 2026 it stopped publishing his back catalogue.

Walliams strongly denies behaving inappropriately. His spokesperson has said he was never told of the allegations or given a chance to respond to the publisher's investigation.
keyFacts: HarperCollins dropped him in December 2025
His back catalogue was dropped in September 2026
He denies all allegations

leftOut.title: Meghan's father Thomas Markle Sr. charged with possessing child abuse material
leftOut.summary:
Thomas Markle Sr., 82, the estranged father of Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, was arrested by the FBI in Florida on 6 November. He is charged with one count of possession of child sexual abuse material, according to the US Attorney's Office. The material was allegedly found in two storage units he rented in the Los Angeles area.

He has not entered a plea, and the allegations have not been tested in court. Meghan described the allegations as deeply disturbing.
keyFacts: Arrested 6 November near Tampa
Charged on a federal criminal complaint
Maximum penalty if convicted: 20 years

leftOut.title: Harry and Meghan speak at European Parliament event on social media harms to children
leftOut.summary:
Prince Harry and Meghan attended an event at the European Parliament in Brussels on 10 November. It opened a memorial installation showing images of 50 children who died after harm they suffered on social media. Parliament President Roberta Metsola was also due to speak.

It was the couple's first public appearance since the allegations against Meghan's father emerged. Harry has campaigned on the risks of social media and AI chatbots for young people.
keyFacts: Event at the European Parliament, Brussels
The installation is called the Lost Screen Memorial
Harry spoke on AI chatbots and children in September

leftOut.title: Treasury Secretary Bessent moved to military base over Iranian threats, sources say
leftOut.summary:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has been moved to live on a military base because of threats from Iran, ABC News (US) reported on Wednesday, citing multiple unnamed sources familiar with the situation. He had reportedly been living in Washington's Georgetown area.

The report said Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio also live on military bases while in Washington. The Secret Service, which protects Bessent, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The move has not been officially confirmed.
keyFacts: The report relies on unnamed sources
ABC News (US) described the story as developing
No official statement had been issued

leftOut.title: Russian strikes kill several people and cut power in eight Ukrainian regions
leftOut.summary:
Russian attacks on 10 and 11 November killed at least four people and injured more than 20 across several Ukrainian regions, according to regional officials cited by Ukrainian news agency UNN. Zaporizhzhia's governor Ivan Fedorov reported one death and 15 injuries, and Donetsk officials reported two deaths.

UNN reported power outages in eight regions, with emergency cuts in Kharkiv after a missile strike damaged garages and cars there. The attacks came as Russian and Ukrainian delegations met for US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi, which ended with a prisoner exchange agreement.
keyFacts: Odesa's governor said a 70-year-old woman died of her injuries
Donetsk officials reported 661 evacuations
Zhytomyr reported damage to energy and transport sites

leftOut.title: Human remains found in sofa dumped in Sydney bushland at Lane Cove North
leftOut.summary:
NSW Police said a man found human remains inside a storage sofa dumped in bushland off Avian Crescent, Lane Cove North, on Wednesday afternoon, the ABC reported. A forensic examination found they were the torso of an adult man. Police said the remains had been there for at least a couple of days.

Superintendent Paul Devaney said police were working to identify the man and find out how he died. He said there was no sign of foul play in Lane Cove and residents were not under threat. Police used a cadaver dog, a line search and aerial surveillance.
keyFacts: The man has not been formally identified
A post-mortem examination will be held
Police are checking the missing persons register

leftOut.title: Man who drove fugitive Hussein Chamas across Australia faces sentencing in Darwin
leftOut.summary:
Irish national Stephen Roche faced a sentencing hearing in the NT Supreme Court on Thursday after pleading guilty to attempting to pervert the course of justice, the ABC reported. He drove fugitive Hussein Chamas about 4,680 kilometres in a rented van before Chamas was intercepted by Border Force in the Arafura Sea.

The prosecution said jail was the only appropriate penalty. Roche's lawyer argued that 123 days already spent on remand was enough, citing his health and remorse. The court heard Roche was to be paid $30,000.
keyFacts: Sentence is due on 1 December
Chamas was jailed in August on drug charges
Roche was arrested in January 2025

leftOut.title: Missing teenager found alive after six nights in Gippsland bush
leftOut.summary:
A 17-year-old who went missing while camping at Walhalla East in Victoria's Gippsland was found alive on Thursday morning, Victoria Police said, according to the ABC. A police helicopter crew spotted him in a dry riverbed about two kilometres east of Stoney Creek.

Police said he had fallen down a steep embankment two days earlier and could not walk. He had cuts and severe sunburn and was taken to Latrobe Regional Hospital. More than 80 volunteers had joined the search, along with police divers, the dog squad and helicopters.
keyFacts: He went missing on 6 November
Walhalla East is about 180 km east of Melbourne
He is being monitored in hospital

leftOut.title: One killed, four injured in shooting at Washington DC gym; gunman dead
leftOut.summary:
A gunman shot five people at and near a gym in Washington DC's Logan Circle neighbourhood on Thursday morning local time, killing one, police said, according to Al Jazeera and CBS News. The area is about 1.6 kilometres north of the White House.

Police said the suspect later died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound after a standoff. Interim Police Chief Jeffery Carroll said the shooting appeared to stem from a dispute with a condominium homeowners association. Nearby schools and apartment buildings were locked down during the search. A local councillor named a suspect, but police had not formally confirmed the identity in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: The shooting began about 8am local time
Federal ATF agents assisted DC police
Police point to a residential dispute as a motive

leftOut.title: Perth inquest hears triple-zero call before 2024 double murder was wrongly graded
leftOut.summary:
A WA coronial inquest has heard that a triple-zero call made before the May 2024 shooting deaths of Jennifer Petelczyc and her daughter Gretl at their Perth home was graded priority two rather than priority one, AAP reported. Counsel assisting said Mark Bombara shot both women and then himself.

WA Police Commander Jason Longhorn told the inquest he believed the priority two grading was incorrect. Superintendent Andrew Wilson said officers had not assessed the risk correctly and that eight officers were disciplined. A lawyer for the family said the women had been targeted as proxies for Bombara's family. The inquest is continuing.
keyFacts: The killings occurred on 24 May 2024
Eight officers were disciplined
The inquest continues

leftOut.title: AFP charges two men over alleged threats to federal politicians
leftOut.summary:
The Australian Federal Police charged two men with using a carriage service to menace, harass or cause offence over alleged threats to politicians, AAP reported. A 43-year-old man was arrested in the Moreton Bay area north of Brisbane on Thursday, and a 67-year-old man was arrested in Melbourne on Wednesday and faces three counts.

Both men were granted conditional bail and are due in court in January and February. AFP Commissioner Krissy Barrett said police charge about one person a week for threatening parliamentarians. The allegations have not been tested in court, and neither man had entered a plea in the reports reviewed.
keyFacts: One man was charged in Queensland, one in Victoria
Both were granted conditional bail
The AFP says it charges about one person a week over such threats

leftOut.title: Trial begins over alleged murder of Quambatook woman in dispute over pool work
leftOut.summary:
Brian Robert Barnes, 68, has pleaded not guilty in the Victorian Supreme Court to murdering 70-year-old Merril Kelly at her home in Quambatook, in north-west Victoria, in January 2025, AAP reported.

Crown prosecutor Patrick Bourke KC alleged Barnes was angry about unpaid pool work and attacked Kelly before taking her body to a cemetery and setting it alight. He said an autopsy showed she died before the fire. Defence barrister David Cronin SC told the jury Barnes did not cause her death and that someone else may have inflicted the fatal injuries. The trial before Justice James Elliott is continuing.
keyFacts: Barnes has pleaded not guilty
Prosecutors allege a dispute over pool work
The trial is continuing

leftOut.title: Pancreatic cancer advocate Cherie Dear named Victorian Australian of the Year
leftOut.summary:
Cherie Dear, who co-founded pancreatic cancer charity Dare to Hope with her late husband, former Hawthorn player Paul Dear, has been named Victoria's 2027 Australian of the Year, ABC News reported.

The other Victorian winners are autism researcher Wenn Lawson as Senior Australian of the Year, Ryan Brigham of Health in Focus as Young Australian of the Year, and Gavin Hynam, who has donated 19 cars to people in need, as Local Hero. The four will join other state and territory recipients in Canberra, where the national winners will be announced on 25 January.
keyFacts: Four Victorian award recipients were named
National awards are on 25 January
State winners become national finalists

leftOut.title: Kalyn Ponga and Stacey Waaka win rugby league's Golden Boot awards
leftOut.summary:
New Zealand's Kalyn Ponga has won the men's International Rugby League Golden Boot for 2026 and compatriot Stacey Waaka won the women's award, AAP reported. The awards were presented at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane on Thursday night.

Ponga broke his forearm in New Zealand's 24-20 World Cup loss to Australia and returned 23 days later. Waaka scored nine tries in four World Cup matches. England's Rob Hawkins won the wheelchair Golden Boot. AAP said voting did not include Sunday's World Cup final.
keyFacts: Ponga is 28
Waaka scored nine World Cup tries
Rob Hawkins won the wheelchair award

leftOut.title: Players' union asks for Socceroos friendly in Jordan to be moved over safety
leftOut.summary:
Professional Footballers Australia has asked Football Australia to reschedule or relocate the Socceroos' planned friendly against Jordan in Amman because of security concerns, AAP reported. PFA chief executive Beau Busch said players overwhelmingly supported the request.

Australia are due to play Qatar in Doha before travelling to Amman four days later. Indonesia has cancelled its 13 November friendly in Amman. AAP said the Asian Cup was postponed after an attack on Riyadh airport attributed to the Houthis. Winger Awer Mabil said he would travel if selected. The squad announcement has been delayed to the weekend.
keyFacts: The PFA wants the match moved or rescheduled
Indonesia cancelled its game in Amman
Football Australia had not announced a decision

leftOut.title: Perth Bears say they are confident of signing Matt Burton
leftOut.summary:
Perth Bears general manager Gareth Holmes said on Thursday he was hopeful of signing Canterbury and NSW State of Origin player Matt Burton within days, AAP reported. Burton had not confirmed any move.

Holmes spoke at the launch of the new NRL club's away jumper at North Sydney Oval and said Burton had decisions to make. Burton visited the club this week. AAP said the Bears can offer a salary-cap allowance of 20 per cent granted by Australian Rugby League Commission chair Peter V'landys in August.
keyFacts: The signing is not confirmed
Burton visited the club this week
The Bears join the NRL as an expansion team

leftOut.title: David Jones staff and union react to planned closure of 19 stores
leftOut.summary:
Thousands of David Jones' 6,000 staff are affected by receivers FTI Consulting's plan, announced on Wednesday, for 19 stores in Australia and New Zealand to trade only until the end of December, AAP reported.

NSW retail union secretary Bernie Smith blamed management decisions for the collapse. Charles Lloyd Jones, a member of the founding family, told AAP that retailers without a distinctive offer were forced to compete on price. The retailer lost $95.5 million in 2024-25. The store closures were reported in an earlier update; this report adds reactions but no new decisions.
keyFacts: 19 stores will close after December
The chain employs about 6,000 people
It lost $95.5m in 2024-25

leftOut.title: Victorian business conditions weakest of any state ahead of election, NAB survey shows
leftOut.summary:
NAB's monthly business survey showed business conditions in Victoria fell to minus 6 in October, the lowest of any state and below the national reading of minus 1, AAP reported. NAB senior economist Gareth Spence linked part of the fall to uncertainty before the 28 November state election.

AAP also cited the Westpac-Melbourne Institute consumer confidence index, which fell 2.7 per cent to a four-year low. Westpac's Matthew Hassan pointed to petrol prices near $2.40 a litre, inflation of 4.3 per cent and the RBA's rate rise to 4.85 per cent. Both surveys were released earlier in the week.
keyFacts: Victorian conditions index: minus 6
National conditions index: minus 1
Consumer confidence is at a four-year low

leftOut.title: Former NSW Liberal MP Rory Amon found guilty of sexually assaulting 13-year-old
leftOut.summary:
A NSW Supreme Court jury found former Pittwater MP Rory Amon guilty of the sexual assault and indecent assault of a 13-year-old boy in 2017, the ABC reported. The jury deliberated for about four hours.

The court heard Amon met the boy through a dating app. Amon had argued he believed the boy was 17. He remains on bail, and sentencing is listed for later this month. At an earlier trial in March, Amon was acquitted of most charges and the jury could not agree on two counts.
keyFacts: The jury deliberated about four hours
The offences occurred in 2017
Sentencing is listed for later this month

leftOut.title: Cummins rejects Khawaja's claim that whole team knew of 2018 ball-tampering plan
leftOut.summary:
Australian Test captain Pat Cummins rejected former teammate Usman Khawaja's claim, made in his memoir, that the entire team knew of the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering plan, the ABC reported. Cummins said he did not know sandpaper was being used.

Cummins said Khawaja had been careless with people's reputations and that legal advice suggested some claims could be defamatory, though he would not take action. He also said the bans given to three players were too harsh. Cricket Australia has ruled out reopening its investigation.
keyFacts: The comments came at a press conference in Sydney
Cricket Australia will not reopen its investigation
Cummins said he would not sue
