leftOut.title: Victoria Police will not charge four Sydney Swans players, citing insufficient evidence
leftOut.summary:
Victoria Police said it would not lay criminal charges against Sydney Swans players Isaac Heeney, Chad Warner, James Jordon and Nick Blakey over an alleged incident at a Melbourne hotel in August, citing insufficient evidence after legal advice, the ABC reported.

Police noted an ongoing civil matter and declined further comment. Swans chief executive Matthew Pavlich said the players could now move forward, and the club said it stood by its decision to stand them down. Lawyers for three women are pursuing civil claims.
keyFacts: Police cited insufficient evidence
The alleged incident occurred in August
Civil claims are continuing

leftOut.title: Prosecutors oppose bail for Darwin teenager charged with terrorism offence
leftOut.summary:
A Darwin teenage girl charged with collecting or making documents likely to facilitate terrorist acts appeared in court on Friday, AAP reported. Prosecutor Hadi Mazloum alleged her diary named a student she wanted dead and that she shared a plan to shoot at a school, and argued the risk to the community was too high for bail.

Her lawyer cited significant psychological circumstances and sought a supervised community-based order. The judge adjourned the bail application to Monday. A 14-year-old boy was arrested with her on 3 November.
keyFacts: She was arrested on 3 November
The arrest followed a joint AFP, NT Police and ASIO operation
Bail will be decided on Monday

leftOut.title: Analysis estimates Victorian Labor has outspent Liberals sixfold on online ads
leftOut.summary:
An analysis by digital campaign platform Populares estimates Victorian Labor and its candidates have spent $3.1 million on online advertising since August, compared with just over $500,000 by the Liberals and about $21,000 by One Nation, the ABC reported. The figures are upper-range estimates from platform disclosures and exclude other media.

The ABC said Labor, the Liberals and the Greens did not respond. An Australia Institute representative said the campaign had seen unprecedented use of AI content and deepfakes.
keyFacts: Labor spending estimated at $3.1 million
Liberal spending just over $500,000
Figures exclude TV and print

leftOut.title: ABC reports US has held talks with Myanmar's military-backed government over rare earths
leftOut.summary:
The Trump administration has held talks with Myanmar's military-backed government ahead of the ASEAN summit in the Philippines, the ABC reported, citing a State Department document that lists countering China and access to rare earth resources among the goals.

The talks followed the detention of a former American Chamber of Commerce head at Yangon airport in June. A Lowy Institute analyst described it as hostage diplomacy, and a human rights advocate criticised the talks. The US has previously accused Myanmar's military of genocide.
keyFacts: China controls about 90 per cent of rare earth output, an analyst said
The ASEAN summit is in the Philippines
The piece is an ABC analysis

leftOut.title: 1960 paper had predicted population would become infinite on 13 November 2026
leftOut.summary:
A 1960 paper in the journal Science predicted world population would approach infinity on 13 November 2026, based on a formula drawn from historical fertility and death rates, the ABC reported. The date was chosen to fall on lead author Heinz von Foerster's birthday.

An economist quoted said the projections held until about the 1980s. Global population growth peaked at about 2.3 per cent a year in 1963, and the UN projects population will peak at just over 10 billion in about 60 years.
keyFacts: The paper was published in 1960
Growth peaked in 1963
The UN projects a peak just over 10 billion

leftOut.title: Olympic cyclist Rohan Dennis admits breaching good behaviour bond
leftOut.summary:
Olympic medallist Rohan Dennis admitted in the South Australian District Court that he breached a good behaviour bond, AAP reported. The bond, imposed in 2025 over the December 2023 crash that killed his wife Melissa Hoskins, carries a suspended 17-month jail term.

Dennis was caught driving while disqualified in June, with two children in the car. Judge Emily Telfer ordered a supervision compliance report and adjourned the matter to 1 February.
keyFacts: The breach was admitted on Friday
The bond carries a 17-month term
The matter returns on 1 February

leftOut.title: Man dies in workplace incident in Adelaide's north-east
leftOut.summary:
A 26-year-old man died at the scene of a workplace incident on Leopold Street, Vista, in Adelaide's north-eastern suburbs on Friday, South Australia Police said, according to the ABC. Emergency services were called at about 12.15pm.

SafeWork SA said it had been notified and sent an investigator and an inspector. SA Power Networks workers were seen examining a power pole nearby. Police will prepare a report for the coroner. No cause has been stated.
keyFacts: The man was 26
SafeWork SA is investigating
A report will go to the coroner

leftOut.title: Guard at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier reprimands Hegseth's group during photos
leftOut.summary:
A video shows a sentinel at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Arlington National Cemetery asking Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth's group to maintain silence and respect while they were laughing during photographs on Veterans Day, Al Jazeera reported.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said the sentinel had responded correctly and that the department honours the military's sacrifices. The incident came a day after House Republicans blocked a vote on articles of impeachment against Hegseth.
keyFacts: The incident was on 11 November
The Pentagon said the guard acted correctly
House Republicans blocked an impeachment vote

leftOut.title: Westpac says it is financing 30 per cent fewer housing construction projects
leftOut.summary:
Westpac chief executive Anthony Miller told a parliamentary inquiry on Thursday that the bank was financing 30 per cent fewer housing construction projects than 18 months ago, and that each dollar lent was delivering fewer homes, AAP reported. He said replacing staff with AI was not the bank's focus.

ANZ chief Nuno Matos said he could not guarantee there would be no job losses from AI. ABS data released on Wednesday showed investor home loans fell a record 30.6 per cent.
keyFacts: Westpac's construction financing is down 30 per cent
CBA and NAB appeared on Friday
Investor loans fell a record 30.6 per cent

leftOut.title: Zelenskyy says Starshield satellite service speeds again restricted
leftOut.summary:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said speed restrictions on Starshield, the military version of the Starlink satellite service, were again hampering Ukraine's interception of Russian jet-powered drones, AAP reported.

The report also restated that Abu Dhabi talks earlier in the week agreed a large prisoner exchange, which Russia's TASS said could happen within two to three weeks. Ukraine said it shot down 89 of 123 drones overnight, and one person was killed in Kyiv. The figures could not be independently verified.
keyFacts: Zelenskyy posted the claim on Thursday
TASS said a swap could come within weeks
Ukraine said 89 of 123 drones were downed

leftOut.title: Rubio says UK and European nations should be part of Ukraine peace talks
leftOut.summary:
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said at a G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris that the UK and other European countries should have a place at negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, AAP reported. He described the Abu Dhabi talks as productive but said much work remained.

Ukraine's president called the talks constructive and substantive, the first since February. Russia's foreign minister Sergei Lavrov said he favoured a broader European security framework being agreed first.
keyFacts: The remarks were made at the G7 in Paris
The Abu Dhabi talks were the first since February
Lavrov wants a wider security framework first

leftOut.title: Former police officer denies desperation in Paddington murder trial evidence
leftOut.summary:
Former NSW police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon, who has pleaded not guilty to murdering Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in February 2024 and claims self-defence, continued his evidence on Thursday, AAP reported.

Under cross-examination about a long message he sent to Baird claiming a cancer diagnosis, he acknowledged parts were untrue but denied being desperate or obsessed. He also admitted posting a false image online about a relationship. The trial continues.
keyFacts: He has pleaded not guilty
Thursday was his sixth day of evidence
The deaths occurred on 19 February 2024

leftOut.title: CBA and NAB chiefs to face parliamentary hearings after fee and wage cases
leftOut.summary:
Commonwealth Bank chief Matt Comyn and NAB chief Andrew Irvine were due to appear before parliamentary hearings on Friday, AAP reported, after NAB agreed to repay $169 million to 66,000 underpaid staff and ASIC began proceedings against CBA over $8.5 million in undisclosed business fees.

Committee chair Ed Husic, a Labor MP, criticised NAB's plans to move about 180 roles offshore. Westpac's chief disclosed a 28 per cent gender pay gap at the hearings.

NAB is repaying $169 million
ASIC is suing CBA over $8.5 million in fees
